decisions.reason: The original real constant conclusion is false for u=i on R under the complex distribution interface. The repair proves constancy in C and retains the real constant conclusion for real u. Mollification constants converge in C; positive-measure ball overlaps and a countable base globalize them. Empty and zero-dimensional domains are handled directly. The three direct item consumers use real BV or real L2 functions, so their actual uses remain valid.

The all-Borel conclusion is valid: the regular-complex definition expressly uses all-Borel regularity, and even finite Radon regularity upgrades to it. The omitted elementary upgrade is now given explicitly using K=C minus G, with each of two errors below epsilon/2; domination transfers it to the difference variation. Compact smooth tests and dominated convergence then determine all Borel masses. Added empty and singleton-domain cases without changing the Statement.

Ordinary Tonelli does not justify coordinate lifts of arbitrary Lebesgue-measurable inputs. The repair uses Borel representatives, proves lifted exceptional sets null by bounded slabs, identifies product and Euclidean integrals, and treats infinite sectional integrals on null sets before induction. Countable Choice is now explicit because the actual completion suppliers require it. Tao Example 1.7.13 and Theorems 1.7.15–1.7.18 were read for the product/completion distinction; the local suppliers specify the Choice scope.

The positive-dimensional shell and rational-ball construction is valid and choice-free, but its cited bump and compactness interfaces require n>=1. Added the missing n=0 singleton construction eta=1 in one covering member, and restricted F1/F3 accurately to n>=1. The original Statement, compact supports, local finiteness and cover subordination are preserved.

Added the n=0 singleton case while preserving the Statement. Also repaired the Step-4 concern: the old unqualified Lebesgue convolution argument relied on measure interfaces requiring Countable Choice. A finite bump-weighted average of sampled values now approximates the compactly supported cutoff function uniformly; a second finite cutoff keeps the denominator positive on its support. The error is at most 2epsilon/3, uses no integration and no countable choice, and preserves complex as well as real C0 functions.

The core partition variation proof is sound, but F1 omitted the elementary upgrade from finite Radon regularity to compact approximation of all Borel sets. Added the explicit C minus G argument and the finite union/intersection argument for the dominating sum lambda. Domination now justifies both approximations in 3.1 and the compact witnesses in 4.1. Countable additivity uses only finitely many near-optimal partitions at a time. Empty vector, empty space and singleton-space cases are explicit; the Statement is unchanged.

F3 and 1.1 explicitly applied the vector-Radon theorem outside its Euclidean domain. The repaired argument defines partition variation on X and proves equality on each Borel A directly. A finite grid partitions the unit sphere into small Borel pieces; projecting the integral of each inverse-image piece onto a unit representative gives V(A)>=(1-epsilon^2/2)lambda(A), while the triangle inequality gives V(A)<=lambda(A). Letting epsilon vanish proves the full claim and measure property, with only finite choice and no Euclidean-domain application.

The complete graph-trace supplier already proves chart independence in Proof 5.1: compare the u=1 flux measures to identify outward normals, then subtract the Green formulas for arbitrary u and use distributional Radon uniqueness plus the unit-density variation calculation to identify traces. Thus assigned F1 and 1.1 cite an actually established supplier result even though its Statement omits the extra compatibility sentence. The remainder glues finitely many charts, derives the zero-extension measure with the correct minus boundary sign, and adds variations on disjoint interior/boundary supports. No edit is needed.

The k=0 terms 1/k and 1/(2k) were undefined. Replaced them by 1/(k+1) and 1/(2(k+1)), and made the partition enumeration j>=1 so the 2^(-j) error weights sum to one. Also specified delta>0, handled empty/singleton domains, and justified the product-measurable absolute-integrable interchanges using positive and negative Tonelli. Local finiteness, the product-rule cancellation, the variation bound and lower semicontinuity still prove the unchanged strict approximation and full-space compact-support claims.
